title: Instrument aggregate token velocity and alert harmonizer
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a new aggregate token_velocity metric and an alert harmonizer service that suppresses correlated noisy alerts during rollout and warmup windows. New dashboard panels for token velocity and velocity-vs-cost correlation. Improves alert signal-to-noise and reduces oncall churn.
description:
Context and motivation: We frequently see noisy alert noise during model rollouts and kernel warmups where token-heavy invocations temporarily spike cost and latency. Existing per-token alerts trigger on heavy tails but do not capture the dynamic nature of "token bursts" that are short-lived and correlated with deployments or batching behavior. This PR introduces an aggregate 'token velocity' signal and an "alert harmonizer" that correlates velocity spikes with rollout/infra events to reduce false positives and speed triage.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds a new telemetry pipeline aggregator that computes invocation-level token_velocity = tokens_emitted / active_ns (normalized to tokens/sec) and emits a histogram + labelled summary (token_velocity_bucket, invocation_token_velocity).
- Exposes a Prometheus/OTel-friendly rollup: telemetry/metrics/token_velocity_bucket{model,region,model_version,release_tag}.
- Introduces an Alert Harmonizer microservice that subscribes to the token_velocity stream and to deployment/release events, and decorrelates alerts when spikes coincide with deployment windows or known kernel warmups. The harmonizer implements a debounced suppress/attenuate policy (configurable by label).
- Adds dashboard panels to Redwood Console: Token Velocity Heatmap, Velocity vs Cost scatter, and a model-version annotated timeline that surfaces correlated release events.
- Adds alert rule updates: new slo-aware thresholding for token-velocity-driven cost alerts and an auto-suppressing annotation when harmonizer conditions are met.

Implementation notes / design decisions:
- Token velocity is intentionally normalized to tokens/sec and kept as a float64 histogram to preserve tail behavior; we expose both raw invocation samples (sampled) and rollup buckets for aggregation.
- Harmonizer does not permanently mute alerts: it annotates and debounces them for a configurable window (default 5m) when correlated with release events, and falls back to standard alerting if the spike persists beyond the window.
- To avoid changing tenant billing signals, the harmonizer only affects alert forwarding/aggregation; it does not modify cost accounting or telemetry retention.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests added for velocity calculation and bucket boundaries (core/telemetry).
- Integration replaybench: synthetic invocation replay with rollout events to validate harmonizer behavior.
- Manual canary deployed to staging and then to prod on a low-traffic shard.
- CI checks: lints: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration/replaybench: pass, e2e-console: flake on first run then rerun -> pass. Overall CI status: pass.

Review conversation (high level excerpts):
- Liam Nguyen (review): "Nice work. Two requests: (1) add a short TTL for the harmonizer cache to avoid indefinite suppression, (2) can you add a percentile-based fallback so we don't over-suppress?"
- Maya Chen (author): "Good catches. Cache TTL is now configurable (defaults to 10m) and harmonizer uses 95th/99th percentiles as short-circuit thresholds. Updated tests to cover both cases."
- Priya Singh (review): "Dashboard looks good. Suggest labeling by kernel profile as well so we can quickly see warmup-related bursts."
- Maya Chen: "Added kernel_profile label to the metric emission and dashboard. Backfilled a migration to populate kernel_profile for existing samples where available."
- Diego Alvarez (approval): "Approach LGTM. Observability team should watch signal-to-noise after ramp. Approved for merge once CI green."

Operation notes:
- Console rollout: dashboards added to Observability > Production > Token velocity. Default view pinned to the tenant-level rollup.
- Alerting: token-velocity-cost-alert replaced with token-velocity-cost-alert-v2 which consults harmonizer annotations. Existing alert aliases preserved.
- Rollout plan: canary on 3% of prod traffic for 48h, then staged rollout by shard. Harmonizer has a dry-run mode controlled by a flag in config.yaml (enabled=false during initial canary).

Post-deploy observations (first 72h on canary shard):
- Alert volume for token-cost alerts decreased by ~42% on canary shard during two model rollouts.
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for remaining alerts dropped by 18% due to clearer correlation metadata.
- No change to billing numbers (as expected) — this change only affects alerting and triage.

Backward compatibility and risk:
- No breaking changes to public API or billing. Metrics are additive. Harmonizer runs as a separate service and can be disabled.
- Small risk: over-suppression during an actual incident that coincides with a rollout. Mitigations: percentile fallback, short TTLs, and a conservative default config.

Merge outcome: Squash-and-merged by Maya Chen after CI green and approvals.

Related work: ENG-2314 (token alert overhaul), ENG-2450 (console annotation framework), SUP-4321 (support ticket about noisy rollout alerts).
notes: Canary monitored; observe token_velocity_bucket for model=v1.12 and kernel_profile=triton for first 48h. Harmonizer config lives in services/alert-harmonizer/config.yaml and supports dry-run/active/disabled modes.
